title: Palindrome Linked List Problem

constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [1, 10^5].
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: The sequence reads the same forward and backward, so the linked list is a palindrome.
The first and last node values differ, so the linked list is not a palindrome.

content.problemStatement:
With the `head` of a singly linked list, output `true` *if it is a* *palindrome* *or* `false` *otherwise*.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/03/03/pal1linked-list.jpg)

```
Input: head = [1,2,2,1]
Output: true
```

**Example 2:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/03/03/pal2linked-list.jpg)

```
Input: head = [1,2]
Output: false
```

**Constraints:**

* The number of nodes in the list is in the range `[1, 10^5]`.
* `0 <= Node.val <= 9`

**Follow up:** Could you do it in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` space?

solution.approach: Find the midpoint using slow/fast pointers, reverse the first half of the list, compare the two halves, and use constant auxiliary space.

better.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
better.description: Use a stack for the first half while traversing with fast/slow pointers, then compare the stack values with the second half.

optimal.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
optimal.description: Use slow/fast pointers to locate the middle, reverse the first half in place, and compare it with the second half. The fast pointer distinguishes even and odd list lengths. This achieves linear time and constant auxiliary space.

bruteForce.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
bruteForce.description: Copy the node values into an array and compare the array with its reverse.

code.Python3:
class Solution:
    def isPalindrome(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> bool:
        if head is None or head.next is None:
            return True
        slow = head
        fast = head
        prev = None
        while fast and fast.next:
            fast = fast.next.next
            nxt = slow.next
            slow.next = prev
            prev = slow
            slow = nxt
        second = slow.next if fast else slow
        first = prev
        while first and second:
            if first.val != second.val:
                return False
            first = first.next
            second = second.next
        return True
